newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS OWNERS DENY PLANS TO FLOAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS OWNERS DENY PLANS TO FLOAT.

text.p: The holding company which owns a majority stake in European soccer champions Juventus denied on Thursday they were about to offer shares to the public following renewed reports of an imminent flotation.

IFI , the holding company of the Agnelli family, issued a statement after the Italian weekly news magazine Panorama said the Fiat vehicle group's stake in Juventus would be taken over by IFI as the prelude to a float.
"The conditions for a bourse listing do not exist for the time being. Therefore any speculation about this is without foundation," the statement said.
News reports that Juventus, who are serie A leaders, and other top Italian clubs could go public have been rife in recent months following successful flotations by British clubs.

However, a flotation in Italy is problematic because most clubs do not meet disclosure rules applicable on the Milan bourse or requirements for three straight years of profit prior to a listing, share analysts say.
Panorama, in an extract of an article to appear in Friday's edition, said IFI would acquire from Fiat the 42 percent stake it does not own by June, taking full control of the club.
It said it was probable that Juventus would choose a foreign stock market for its debut, adding that the most likely coordinator of the operation was Salomon Brothers.
Defending champions AC Milan have also been reported to be considering a stock market float. The club is owned by billionaire media mogul and opposition Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi.
